items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Corollary 11.2.16 at source lines 648-655: the Dedekind reals are Dedekind complete, i.e. every real-valued Dedekind cut has a unique real with the prescribed lower and upper classes. The author's proof (source lines 657-664) is a three-step argument that cannot be shortened: it first invokes the retained admissibility lemma for the Dedekind completion (line 658), then applies the retained finality theorem to get embeddings in both directions (lines 659-660), and then has to show that these embeddings are inverse to each other by the rigidity argument that an order-preserving field homomorphism fixing the dense rational subfield is the identity (lines 660-662) before the completeness statement follows (line 663). The statement records only the completeness property; the two labelled inputs and the rigidity step are invisible in it.
